{{Use mdy dates|date=April 2015}} {{Infobox Election | election_name = United States House of Representatives elections in New Mexico, 2018 | country = New Mexico | type = legislative | ongoing = yes | previous_election = United States House of Representatives elections in New Mexico, 2016 | previous_year = 2016 | next_election = United States House of Representatives elections in New Mexico, 2020 | next_year = 2020 | seats_for_election = All three New Mexico seats to the [[United States House of Representatives]] | election_date = {{Start date|2018|11|06}} | party1 = Democratic Party (United States) | last_election1 = 2 | seats1 = | seat_change1 = | popular_vote1 = | percentage1 = | swing1 = | party2 = Republican Party (United States) | last_election2 = 1 | seats2 = | seat_change2 = | popular_vote2 = | percentage2 = | swing2 = | map_image = | map_caption = }} {{ElectionsNM}} The '''2018 United States House of Representatives elections in New Mexico''' will be held on November 6, 2018, to elect the three [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Representatives]] from the [[U.S. state|state]] of [[New Mexico]], one from each of the state's three [[New Mexico's congressional districts|congressional districts]]. The elections will coincide with the [[New Mexico gubernatorial election, 2018|gubernatorial election]], as well as [[United States House of Representatives elections, 2018|other elections]] to the House of Representatives, [[United States Senate elections, 2018|elections]] to the [[United States Senate]] and various [[United States elections, 2018#State elections|state]] and [[United States elections, 2018#Local elections|local elections]]. {{Toclimit|limit=2}} ==District 1== {{See also|New Mexico's 1st congressional district}} Democrat [[Michelle Lujan Grisham]], who has represented the district since 2013, was reelected to a third term with 65% of the vote in 2016. Lujan Grisham is not running for reelection and will instead [[New Mexico gubernatorial election, 2018|run for Governor of New Mexico]].{{cite news|url=https://www.abqjournal.com/908217/u-s-rep-michelle-lujan-grisham-announces-2018-gubernatorial-bid.html|title=U.S. Rep. Michelle Lujan Grisham announces 2018 gubernatorial bid|work=[[Albuquerque Journal]]|last=Boyd|first=Dan|date=December 13, 2016|accessdate=December 13, 2016}} New Mexico's 1st district is one of 36 Democrat-held House districts targeted by the [[National Republican Congressional Committee]] in 2018.{{cite web|url=https://www.nrcc.org/2017/02/08/nrcc-announces-initial-offensive-targets-2018-cycle/|title=NRCC Announces Initial Offensive Targets For The 2018 Cycle - NRCC|date=February 8, no change | votes = | percentage = }} {{Election box end}} ==District 2== {{See also|New Mexico's 2nd congressional district}} Republican [[Steve Pearce (politician)|Steve Pearce]], who has represented the district since 2011 and previously represented the district from to 2003 to 2009, was reelected to a fourth consecutive and seventh total term with 63% of the vote in 2016. Pearce is not running for reelection, instead running for Governor of New Mexico. New Mexico's 2nd district is one of the 80 Republican-held seats that the [[Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee]] is targeting in
